units.label: SteerConf共用操作与计分
units.description: 同一题的五个信心操纵提示产生回答—信心对，聚合并选择最终回答；五级是同题条件而非五项独立行为实验。

units.label: 主模型与基线比较
units.description: 七个数据集、三主模型，有/无CoT；五任务子集比较采样基线及组件消融，引用U01。

units.label: 分布诊断与操纵分析
units.description: 对生成信心按正确性及提示等级绘图，比较均值及加方向符号的分布距离，非新的人类实验。

units.label: 附录稳健性与选择变体
units.description: 逐提示移除、简短提示、五比三等级、小模型及多数选择变体；子集不同，不能并为统一重复测量次数。

facts.statement: 研究目标是用黑箱提示直接引出口头信心，改善信心与正确率的校准及正确/错误回答的区分；SteerConf不访问内部logits，也不新增训练或微调。

method_function.text: 界定被测构念与本文操作范围

facts.statement: 一次题目在五级提示下分别回答，五对输出进入同一次聚合；主比较与附录变体共享框架，但模型、任务子集及表中结果不完全相同，不能把每提示当独立实验或假定各表为同一运行。

method_function.text: 对齐题目、提示、模型和变体层次

facts.statement: 主实验七任务为Sports Understanding、StrategyQA、GSM8K、Date Understanding、Object Counting、MMLU Law与Business Ethics，覆盖常识、算术、符号、专业及伦理知识。

method_function.text: 固定材料与任务范围

facts.statement: 主模型为GPT-3.5、GPT-4、LLaMA3；LLaMA3使用70B、4bit量化。分别比较vanilla口头信心及CoT条件；正文另报GPT-4 API费用约1500美元。

method_function.text: 模型与推理条件

facts.statement: 主设置ℓ=2，提示索引−2到2为very cautious/cautious/vanilla/confident/very confident；每题每级引出一个回答与一个信心，理论分值0–1，实际提示要求0–100数值百分比。

method_function.text: 操纵方向与强度并收集配对输出

facts.statement: CoT版要求step-by-step Explanation后给限定ANSWER_TYPE和信心；non-CoT版只回答与信心、不解释。谨慎提示要求避免错答高信心，极谨慎再要求几乎都低；自信提示要求避免对答低信心，极自信再要求几乎都高。vanilla只定义信心并索取格式。

method_function.text: 提示内容操纵及CoT条件

facts.statement: 对同题2ℓ+1个信心取算术均值μ；σ为离均差平方和除2ℓ+1后开根号（主设置分母5），κconf=1/(1+σ/μ)。这是跨提示总体SD与变异系数变换，不是样本SD、SE或κ一致性检验。

method_function.text: 度量跨操纵信心稳定性

facts.statement: 对同题各回答计相同回答次数，freq(y)=该次数/(2ℓ+1)，κans取最大频率；最终信心c=μ×κans×κconf。最大频率是众数比例，未进行机会校正。

method_function.text: 结合回答一致性与信心一致性下调均值

facts.statement: 原文选择器先取cmin/min(cl)、cmax/max(cl)，j=floor[(c−cmin)/(cmax−cmin)×(2ℓ+1)]；随后仅写j<−ℓ时选f−ℓ，−ℓ≤j≤ℓ时选fj。未给j>ℓ、全等信心的分支，也未写索引减ℓ平移。

method_function.text: 将聚合信心映射到某级回答

facts.statement: 附录ECE把N题按信心等宽分B箱，区间((b−1)/B,b/B]；每箱正确率与平均信心之差取绝对值，按箱题数/N加权求和。原文未给实际B与空箱/零信心处理。

method_function.text: 样本数加权的校准误差

facts.statement: 附录把正确指标I(f(x)=y)作标签并写AUROC=∫TPR dFPR；但印刷TPR和FPR均以全部N为分母，分子各为信心≥阈值且正确或错误的计数。该式与通常按正/负类数归一不同，实际代码未核实。

method_function.text: 区分论文命名指标与印刷计算式

facts.statement: 附录PR-P以正确回答为正类、PR-N以错误为正类；PR-P precision=阈值上正确数/阈值上总数、recall=阈值上正确数/全部正确数，再对PR曲线积分。PR-N仅称替换正确指标，未说明反转信心分值；正文却将PR-P/PR-N对应错误/正确，正类说明冲突。

method_function.text: 明确PR指标正类、分母及来源差别

facts.statement: 基线均用CoT的GPT-3.5和LLaMA3：Self-Random同提示重复M=5；Misleading以误导信息挑战最初回答并观察稳定性、M=5；Top-K一次回答给K=5个候选—信心对。前二使用引用的Consistency聚合，Top-K使用Pair-Rank。

method_function.text: 比较抽样/误导/单次候选与SteerConf

facts.statement: LLaMA3 CoT在GSM8K/Law/DateUnd/StrategyQA/Ethics进行组件消融：移除steering，替换聚合为Consistency或Avg-Conf，或同时移除两者成Self-Random加两聚合；表4与表9另外组合Misleading/Self-Random/Top-K的聚合方案。

method_function.text: 操纵框架部件及替代聚合作对照

facts.statement: 主表以百分数报告ECE、AUROC、PR-N、PR-P及跨任务平均；例如无CoT GPT-3.5平均ECE41.8→20.7。改善并非逐格成立，如CoT LLaMA3在GSM8K ECE5.0→7.8，表3 Self-Random的GSM8K ECE2.2也优于SteerConf6.1。

method_function.text: 记录结果汇总并避免全条件优势外推

facts.statement: 图3为LLaMA3 CoT五任务×四方法的信心直方图，横轴信心、纵轴样本数，蓝/红区分对/错；图4比较Law/Sport/ObjCnt/StrategyQA的vanilla与SteerConf信心分布及可靠性图。

method_function.text: 可视化同批输出的信心—正确性关系

facts.statement: 作者将更连续均匀的信心分布、正确错误分离及校准信心与正确率对齐解释为方法有效；未报告分布拟合检验或这些机制的因果识别。

method_function.text: 明确图形解释的认识地位

facts.statement: 表5用GPT-3.5无CoT，按0–100%区间、箱宽5形成离散信心分布，逐steering与vanilla比较Mean、Wasserstein Distance、Jensen–Shannon Divergence；为表示方向，将Mean差符号附加到本来非负的距离/散度。

method_function.text: 量化操纵后分布位移

facts.statement: 图5显示LLaMA3 CoT五任务五级信心分布；另GPT-3.5无CoT的表5分析指出极端提示方向较明显，而中等confident可反向，如Ethics均值较vanilla低1.79。

method_function.text: 检查提示操纵并保留不完全服从

facts.statement: 逐提示消融一次从五级删除一个，LLaMA3 CoT五任务表6；另表10分别只用very cautious/cautious/vanilla/confident/very confident与完整聚合比较。

method_function.text: 区分移除单提示与单提示运行

facts.statement: 附录比较五级与三级提示，LLaMA3 CoT：no_verys删除very cautious和very confident，no_mild删除cautious和confident。附录将级数记ℓ=5/3，与正文用ℓ=2代表五级的符号不同。

method_function.text: 检验查询成本与等级数量取舍

facts.statement: GPT-3.5比较原版与brief提示；作者称保留核心steering意图、缩短表达，示例very cautious删去重要决策与避免错答高信心的长说明，改成每答倾向很低信心。表7报告五任务ECE/AUROC。

method_function.text: 测试简化措辞后的稳健性

facts.statement: Qwen3-1.7b附加CoT实验因Law/Ethics信心格式频繁失效而不报告两任务，仅报告GSM8K、Sport、DateUnd、StrategyQA、ObjCnt。

method_function.text: 限定小模型可用输出的比较范围

facts.statement: Qwen表8平均ECE35.5→31.2、AUC58.8→63.6，但Sport/DateUnd/StrategyQA的ECE与AUROC均变差；brief表7也非每任务优于原版，如StrategyQA ECE21.0对14.9。故不能把作者‘consistently’读为逐任务优势。

method_function.text: 限定附录结果的概括范围

facts.statement: SteerConf(Majority)只将最终答案选择换为最常见回答，频次并列时选并列答案中平均steered信心最高者；剩余完全并列未报告。表12比较两模型CoT七任务的准确率及四信心指标。

method_function.text: 检验选择器的校准—准确率取舍

facts.statement: 表12 LLaMA3跨任务平均准确率为vanilla83.1%、原SteerConf82.3%、Majority83.6%；对应ECE11.1/7.3/7.8。作者据此推荐校准优先或准确率优先的变体，是结果相关建议而非新增操作。

method_function.text: 记录替代选择器的性能取舍

facts.statement: 作者清单明确未做误差条/统计显著性测试，理由为重复API成本；因此表中的significant字样与单次汇总不构成显著性检验或不确定区间。

method_function.text: 标明实际未实施的验证

facts.statement: 作者限制为提示手工设计、多次查询增加成本、当前聚焦数值或多选任务；自动/自适应提示及开放式任务是未来工作，不是已执行控制。

method_function.text: 限定适用性与未来方法

evidence.quote:
Verbalized Confidence. Confidence represents a model’s certainty in its predictions, typically
expressed as a probability (e.g., "80% confidence"). A score closer to 1 indicates high certainty, while
a score near 0 reflects uncertainty. However, for large language models (LLMs), internal confidence
scores are not directly accessible due to their black-box nature. Instead, confidence is elicited through
verbalized responses obtained via prompting, where the model explicitly states its confidence in
natural language (e.g., "I am 80% confident in answer A") [38, 31].
Verbalized Confidence Elicitation. This process involves modifying the original query prompt to
explicitly request confidence scores from LLMs. For example, given the question "Which one is
bigger, 9.8 or 9.10? Provide your answer," the prompt can be rephrased as "Which one is bigger, 9.8
or 9.10? Provide your answer along with your confidence (%)." The model might then respond with
"9.8, 80%" instead of just "9.8," thereby verbalizing its confidence level as 80%.
Confidence Calibration and Failure Prediction. Verbalized confidence scores elicited from LLMs
are often miscalibrated, meaning the reported confidence does not accurately reflect the true likelihood
of correctness. For instance, a model might state "80% confidence" for answers that are correct only
50% of the time. Confidence calibration addresses this issue by aligning the model’s confidence
scores with the actual accuracy of predictions [11]. Ideally, predictions with 80% confidence should
exhibit 80% accuracy. This is crucial for applications where confidence scores guide decision-making,
such as in medical diagnosis or autonomous driving. The effectiveness of confidence calibration is
commonly evaluated using metrics such as ECE. Failure prediction focuses on identifying incorrect
predictions by leveraging confidence scores. It is formulated as a binary classification task, where
correct predictions are labeled as 0 and incorrect ones as 1. The performance of failure prediction
is measured using AUROC, which assesses the model’s ability to rank incorrect predictions below
correct ones [1]. Detailed computations and evaluations are provided in the experiments.

Our Contributions. We propose SteerConf, a novel framework that leverages the steerability of
LLMs’ confidence scores to enhance their reliability. SteerConf comprises three key components:
(1) We propose a steering prompt strategy to guide LLMs in generating confidence scores in a
specified direction (e.g., conservative or optimistic) by employing prompts with varying steering
intensities. For each question, we sample multiple responses, capturing both answers and their
associated confidence scores across different steering levels. (2) We introduce a steered confidence
consistency measure to evaluate the alignment of confidence scores across multiple steered responses,
leveraging this consistency to enhance confidence calibration. (3) We design a steered confidence
calibration method that leverages the consistency measures to aggregate confidence scores and applies
linear quantization to identify the most reliable answer based on the calibrated confidence. SteerConf
is a simple yet effective framework that can be directly applied to existing LLMs without requiring
additional training or fine-tuning.

In our setting, we set ℓ = 2, which means we have five steering levels: {very cautious, cautious,
vanilla, confident, very confident}, a moderate granularity, which is sufficient to demonstrate the
effectiveness of our method. Our framework is flexible and can be extended to more steering levels

In this section, we analyze the impact of the answer selection mechanism in the SteerConf method.
We denote SteerConf (Majority) as a variant of SteerConf, where the answer selection is replaced
with a majority voting mechanism [38]. Specifically, in SteerConf (Majority), the final answer
is determined by the most frequent response. In cases of ties, the answer with the highest mean
steered confidence score among the tied responses is selected. The results in Table 12 demonstrate

(3) Symbolic Reasoning covering Date Understanding (DateUnd) [36] and Object Counting (ObjCnt) [33]; (4) Professional Knowledge tested through Law (Law) from MMLU [12]; and (5) Ethical

quantify this, we first compute the mean confidence µc of the steered confidences {cl (x)}ℓl=−ℓ as in
Eq. (1), representing the average certainty level, and the standard deviation σc in Eq. (2), measuring
how consistently this certainty is maintained across steering levels from −ℓ to ℓ. Intuitively, higher
µc with lower σc indicates stronger confidence consistency.
Intuitively, the ratio µσcc , known as the coefficient of variation, naturally normalizes the dispersion
of a distribution relative to the mean, showing the extent of variability in relation to the mean of
the observations. A smaller value of µσcc indicates that the data points tend to be very close to the
mean and are more consitent, while a larger value indicates that the data points are spread out over

In this section, we analyze the impact of the answer selection mechanism in the SteerConf method.
We denote SteerConf (Majority) as a variant of SteerConf, where the answer selection is replaced
with a majority voting mechanism [38]. Specifically, in SteerConf (Majority), the final answer
is determined by the most frequent response. In cases of ties, the answer with the highest mean
steered confidence score among the tied responses is selected. The results in Table 12 demonstrate
the calibration effectiveness of our approach. For instance, with LLaMA3, the average ECE for
SteerConf is 7.3%, compared to 7.8% for SteerConf (Majority). Similarly, for GPT-3.5, the average
PR-N metric for SteerConf is 62.0%, significantly outperforming SteerConf (Majority) at 53.9%.

Table 12: Performance comparison across datasets for SteerConf variants with different answer

Table 12 also highlights the trade-off between calibration and accuracy. While SteerConf achieves
superior calibration compared to vanilla verbalized confidence elicitation, it incurs a slight reduction
in accuracy. Conversely, SteerConf (Majority) offers marginally better accuracy than SteerConf but
at the expense of slightly weaker calibration. For example, with LLaMA3, the average accuracy of
SteerConf is 82.3%, compared to 83.6% for SteerConf (Majority), while vanilla LLaMA3 achieves
83.1%. In summary, SteerConf is recommended for scenarios prioritizing calibration, while SteerConf
(Majority) is better suited for applications where accuracy is more critical.

In this paper, we introduced SteerConf, a framework for improving LLM confidence reliability
through semantic steering. Our approach addresses the critical issue of overconfidence, which
undermines trustworthiness in high-stakes applications. By leveraging carefully designed prompts,
we systematically steer LLM confidence in desired directions. The framework comprises three key
components: a steering prompt strategy, a steered confidence consistency measure, and a steered
confidence calibration method. Together, these components enhance confidence calibration without
requiring model internals or fine-tuning. Comprehensive evaluations across seven benchmarks with
state-of-the-art LLMs demonstrate consistent improvements over existing methods. This work has
significant implications for deploying LLMs in critical domains where reliable confidence estimation
is essential. By offering an effective black-box approach, SteerConf enables trustworthy AI without
requiring specialized expertise or access to model internals.
Limitations and Future Work. It is common to mannually design prompts for LLMs, and our
method is no exception. Future work will explore automatic prompt generation to address this.
Additionally, using multiple prompts increases computational costs; we aim to develop adaptive
strategies to optimize prompt usage based on task and model needs. Following prior work, our current
tasks focus on numerical answers (GSM8K) or multiple-choice questions (Law), where ambiguity is
minimal and answer consistency is both sufficient and effective. Extending to more open-ended tasks
is an important future direction.

LLM Models. We evaluate several widely-used LLMs: GPT-3.5 [28], LLaMA3 [10], and GPT-4 [29].
LLaMA3 is used in its 70B parameter version with 4-bit quantization. Note that experiments with
GPT-4 incurred a cost of approximately 1500 USD due to its higher pricing. We first compare
these LLMs using vanilla verbalized confidence elicitation, and then evaluate each LLM with CoT
prompting [35] for confidence elicitation. Results are reported in Table 1 and Table 2 in Section 4.2.
Details on the application of CoT are provided in Appendix B.
